title: The draft picks, deals and bets behind the race
intro: Jaxon The Box won the Week 8 meeting with Lamarley & Me to take sole possession of first. Smith-Njigba is returning first-round value, but the supporting stories go much deeper: Matthew Stafford in the tenth, Chuba Hubbard in the eighth, and Jordan Love off waivers. September’s trades are still shaping Sundays. Here is what each manager has put on the field through eight weeks—and the decisions that deserve more attention than the win-loss column allows.
source: Reporting covers Weeks 1–8 of the 2026 Madden Curse season. Player totals count actual starts for that fantasy team, not bench points or NFL season totals. Draft ownership, September trades, and archived acquisitions were checked against the local league records on November 3, 2026.

teams.name: Jaxon The Box
teams.headline: JSN WAS THE PLAN.
teams.article: Naming the team after Jaxon Smith-Njigba looks less like fandom and more like an investment thesis. The first-round pick has delivered 187.96 points across eight starts, with Christian Watson adding 125.80 from a fifth-round draft slot and Trey McBride contributing every week. That supporting cast matters: this is not a contender waiting for one receiver to rescue it. Smith-Njigba supplied 118 receiving yards and a touchdown in the Week 8 win over Lamarley & Me, the result that put Jaxon alone at 6–2. The name gets the attention. The depth makes the lead credible.

teams.name: Lamarley & Me
teams.headline: WARREN WAS A STEAL.
teams.article: The fifth round is where Lamarley & Me found a second engine. Jaylen Warren has put 128.30 points into the starting lineup, almost matching second-rounder Kyren Williams at 133.50. Those are two distinct draft investments doing the work together, not one star dragging the roster uphill. Even the Week 8 loss contained a warning for the field: Tee Higgins went for 155 receiving yards and two touchdowns, while Warren rushed for 143 yards and a score. Losing the head-to-head with Jaxon cost Lamarley the shared lead. It did not erase the running-back foundation that makes another run entirely believable.

teams.name: WE SELL EXTENDED WARREN-TY
teams.headline: ALLEN. CHASE. PROBLEMS.
teams.article: WARREN-TY did more than draft a quarterback and hope. Josh Allen has produced 192.32 points in seven starts, Kenneth Walker III has supplied another 149.10, and the September 15 deal brought Ja’Marr Chase into the picture. That trade still has a very visible payoff: Chase caught 11 passes for 141 yards and a touchdown in Week 8, alongside Allen’s three combined passing and rushing touchdowns. Together they powered the rebound against Gibbs Me TDs. This is also the roster that has beaten both Jaxon and Lamarley. When the manager goes shopping, the rest of the league has reason to read the fine print.

teams.name: Let Romo Take the Wheel
teams.headline: BUILT IN THE MIDDLE.
teams.article: The middle of Romo’s draft has been doing heavyweight work. Third-rounder Javonte Williams and fourth-rounder Bucky Irving have combined for 248.80 starting-lineup points through eight weeks, giving this team something sturdier than a collection of famous receivers. Irving’s 170 rushing yards and touchdown helped secure the Week 8 win over Bo-Bo; Puka Nacua added 11 catches and a score. That was Romo’s fourth win in five games. The run is easier to understand when you look past the team name: this manager built a backfield that keeps creating ways to win, even when one of its pieces has a quiet Sunday.

teams.name: Am I COOKed? 👨🏽‍🍳
teams.headline: SWIFT’S KITCHEN NOW.
teams.article: James Cook may be on the sign, but D’Andre Swift has been doing the heaviest lifting. The fourth-round pick leads this starting lineup with 138.70 points, ahead of Cook’s 125.70 in seven appearances. Swift’s three rushing touchdowns in Week 8 were the clearest expression of that return on investment: the manager did not need the first-round pick to do everything. There is substance behind the 5–3 record, too. COOKed has already beaten WARREN-TY and Lamarley, and the win over Something Burrowed survived Joe Burrow’s huge afternoon on the other side. This kitchen has more than one reliable burner.

teams.name: Sausage Egg McCaffrey 🍳
teams.headline: LOVE, FROM THE WIRE.
teams.article: The useful name on Sausage’s transaction sheet is Jordan Love. Claimed off waivers on September 23, Love has delivered 120.56 points in six starts for Sausage, including three passing touchdowns in Week 8. Christian McCaffrey and Ashton Jeanty remain the foundation, but finding a starting quarterback without spending a draft pick on him has given this team another route to points. The Week 8 loss to Aura interrupted a pair of emphatic wins. It did not remove Sausage from the league’s top three offenses—or undo the value of answering a roster need on waivers.

teams.name: Chat Take the Wheel 👾
teams.headline: STAFFORD. ROUND TEN.
teams.article: Matthew Stafford in the tenth round is the sort of draft decision that deserves a second look at midseason. He has started all eight games for Chat and contributed 139.64 points, providing an answer at quarterback without a premium pick. Week 8 showed the backfield’s answer, too: Tony Pollard rushed for 117 yards and two touchdowns, while Josh Jacobs scored on the ground and through the air. That combination helped pull Chat back to 4–4. The earlier schedule delivered some ugly assignments, but there is a difference between surviving on luck and finding production from several parts of a roster. Chat has evidence of the latter.

teams.name: OBJ - AuraFarming
teams.headline: MAYE CHANGED THE MOOD.
teams.article: Aura’s season did not end with the 0–4 start. One of the manager’s most consequential moves came in the September 18 trade with Gibbs: Drake Maye arrived in a package that also included A.J. Brown, Isaiah Likely and the Rams defense. Maye has since appeared in four starting lineups here and produced 114.16 points. In Week 8, his three combined passing and rushing touchdowns complemented Bhayshul Tuten’s 104 rushing yards and two total touchdowns. The result was a third win in four games. That is a more interesting comeback than the record alone suggests: the manager changed the roster, and different players started changing Sundays.

teams.name: Something Burrowed👰🏻‍♀️
teams.headline: BURROW STILL HAS THAT.
teams.article: Joe Burrow’s Week 8 line was almost rude: 462 passing yards, five passing touchdowns and a rushing score. The 42.48 fantasy points did not beat COOKed, but they made it difficult to dismiss the roster’s upside. There is a quieter piece of draft work underneath that headline. Brock Purdy, selected in the thirteenth round, has supplied 91.14 points across four starts, while first-rounder Jonathan Taylor has contributed in all eight weeks. Those backup-quarterback points count just as much as the spectacular ones. Burrowed has already climbed out of a 1–4 opening; a manager getting useful starts from both an early investment and a late-round alternative has something to keep building on.

teams.name: Gibbs Me TDs
teams.headline: BOWERS WAS THE MOVE.
teams.article: The September 18 trade put Brock Bowers in a Gibbs jersey, and Week 8 supplied an easy explanation for the attraction: seven catches, 92 yards and two touchdowns. Jahmyr Gibbs added 153 rushing yards and a score of his own. Losing to WARREN-TY with those performances is frustrating, but it is not evidence that the core has stopped working. Gibbs has 178.80 points in seven starts, and the Bowers deal added a genuine receiving centerpiece rather than another interchangeable lineup option. The three-game skid needs an answer. This roster has already shown a 4–1 version of itself, and the manager has put real talent in position to rediscover it.

teams.name: Honey Bijan
teams.headline: DAK IN THE EIGHTH.
teams.article: Honey’s first-round identity is Bijan Robinson, but the eighth-round quarterback has earned a place in the story. Dak Prescott has supplied 134.84 points in seven starts, close to Robinson’s 140.80 across eight. That is useful production from a much later investment, and a reason to give the draft more credit than the 2–6 record invites. Honey has faced the most points in the league through Week 8, including several opponents’ outsized afternoons. The Week 7 win over COOKed showed the other side of the equation: this roster can deliver a convincing result when its pieces land together. The manager did find value; the schedule has not been generous about rewarding it.

teams.name: Bo-Bo Milk Tea
teams.headline: HUBBARD. ROUND EIGHT.
teams.article: CeeDee Lamb is the obvious headline, but Chuba Hubbard is the draft receipt worth keeping. An eighth-round pick has contributed 99.80 points in six starts, including 122 rushing yards and two touchdowns in the Week 4 win over Aura. Bo-Bo also kept working at quarterback: Kirk Cousins was added as a free agent on October 14 and produced four combined touchdowns in Week 8. That loss to Romo was not the desired payoff, yet the lineup decision brought 28.18 points. Add the Week 7 upset of WARREN-TY, and this is not a roster without answers. There have been fewer wins than the manager wanted, but some of the best evidence of good process sits outside the standings.

pickups.method: Each pickup removed from the weeks his team started him, his slot refilled by the owner's best bench player by Yahoo projection, else the best waiver pick; points added = his score minus the stand-in's.
